name: surprises-2
statement: The functional part of the RL-Zero-Math weight change is a low-rank, near-linear shift (a few coherent singular directions per matrix, dense across neurons, that write a deliberation/answer-format readout into the residual stream), while the high-rank remainder that holds most of the change energy is optimizer noise that does almost nothing; so neuron subsets fail (each holds only its proportional share of the dense low-rank part), DARE works (it preserves the low-rank part in expectation and adds only high-rank noise), and RL leaves neuron features unchanged on general text.
scope: Olmo-3-1025-7B base vs Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math (step 2,800), all 2-D weight matrices; MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 (n13 setting) and T 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3. Does not cover SFT deltas, the 1B Bolmo grafts, other model families, or the cue and sampling results.

explains.quote: 11.8% of its squared norm sits in 8 singular directions per matrix
explains.how: The delta has a low-rank head 15-20x above a Gaussian null: the coherent part the theory says carries the function.

explains.quote: Late-MLP top directions x base lm_head read as deliberation words
explains.how: The top singular directions read out as the deliberation and format tokens that recovering arms adopt.
Top-changed neurons score like random neurons because the functional low-rank part is spread evenly over neurons.
DARE keeps the expected delta, so its low-rank projection survives while the added noise is high-rank.

explains.quote: yet it scores like the whole MLP delta
explains.how: 33-1,000x the change energy costs nothing, which only holds if the function lives in a low-dimensional projection the noise barely touches.

explains.quote: Every arm that recovers accuracy also takes RL's format and length
explains.how: Recovery is all-or-none along one format/length readout, as expected from a few shared directions.

explains.quote: the RL change is NOT concentrated in MLP neurons
explains.how: A dense low-rank direction has no small neuron support.

explains.quote: 88 % of all 352,256 neurons have a positive score
explains.how: Almost every neuron carries a small piece of the same directions, and the pieces add linearly.
A small shift along a fixed subspace acts to first order, so per-neuron contributions sum.

explains.quote: RL barely moves which tokens a neuron fires on most
explains.how: A low-rank readout shift does not re-organise neuron features, so top-activating contexts are unchanged.

explains.quote: diverge on math solutions, more with depth
explains.how: The shift directions are engaged only by deliberation contexts and accumulate through the residual stream with depth.
Most entries move by rounding-level amounts: the high-rank noise part of the delta.

explains.quote: Mean KL per token after the cue 0.06-0.09 nats
explains.how: The output change is small and spread over many positions (top 4 % carry only 38.7 % of KL), as a global low-rank shift produces.

conflicts.how: DARE copies of a fine-tune delta destroy the 1B Bolmo model; the theory needs that SFT delta to have far more norm or be higher-rank, which is not measured.
A linear shift predicts a monotone dose curve up to 1; the peak below 1 (on an SFT delta) does not fit.

conflicts.quote: Edit minus norm-matched random: +1.7 points [-1.7, +5.0], not separated
conflicts.how: On a cap-limited model a random edit gives most of the gain, so directionless perturbation can also raise accuracy.
The published view is that RL updates are full-rank; the theory claims full-rank energy but low-rank function.
Energy is spread over many components; the theory must hold that energy and function come apart.

rival: Diffuse full-rank function: every entry contributes a little and the low-rank head is incidental. It predicts that a rank-8 truncation of each matrix's delta recovers only about its 11.8 % energy share of the gain (near base, like the top-10 % neuron arms) and that the high-rank remainder recovers most of it; this theory predicts the opposite.

predictions.experiment: Base + rank-8 SVD truncation of (RL - base) in every 2-D matrix, plain prompt, MATH-500 n=500, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, cap 16,384, grader v3, one sample (endpoints v3: base 305, RL 464)
predictions.refuted_by: fewer than 390 right, or 'Answer:' line in more than 15 % of answers (base-like format)

predictions.experiment: Base + (delta minus its rank-8 truncation) in every 2-D matrix, same setting
predictions.refuted_by: 410 or more right: the high-rank remainder would then carry the gain

predictions.experiment: Base + random rank-8 update per matrix with the same per-matrix Frobenius norm as the rank-8 truncation, same setting
predictions.refuted_by: 350 or more right: any low-rank perturbation of that norm would then give the gain

predictions.experiment: Base + rank-1 SVD truncation of (RL - base) in every 2-D matrix, same setting
Base + 0.5 * (RL - base), plain prompt, MATH-500 n=500, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, cap 16,384, grader v3
predictions.refuted_by: fewer than 370 right (no wide plateau along the direction)
